rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.5 and Tables 3-11: own field spectro-radiometer measurements (414 leaf samples, four varieties, PACA region, 2016) with GA-selected spectral disease indices classified by SVM and compared with twelve common SVIs.
rows.notes: The study supports the detection part of the passage: SDIs gave higher classification accuracy than complete spectra and common SVIs in most cases (Tables 9-11 vs 6-8; e.g. August 100% for three varieties with SDIs vs 90-97% for best SVIs), measured on leaves in production vineyards. However the row's function is pest_control and the study only detects/discriminates FD; it reports no result on disease control, management action or loss avoidance, so Q2 is no and upstream is set. Had the claim been rated as detection only: Q3 no (single method, SVM cross-validated classification; PCR/inspector used only as ground truth), Q4 no (pigment mechanisms discussed, not measured), Q5 no (one region, four cultivars of one crop), Q6 no (leaf scale only), Q7 no (dependence on severity and variety is reported as variation, not a stated requirement), Q8 would be yes (Section 4: leaf scale only, symptomatic leaves only, no test against Bois Noir, other varieties/environments/scales needed, no single best index), Q9 no (10-fold CV means only, no dispersion).

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.5 and Tables 3-11: own field spectral measurements of healthy and FD-infected grapevine leaves and classification experiments with SDIs versus SVIs.
rows.notes: The study reports only detection/classification accuracy of FD on leaves; it contains no measurement of yield, fruit quality or production losses and no result linking detection to avoided losses. Yield losses from FD are mentioned only from the literature in the Introduction. Crop production effect is therefore not evidenced; the study is upstream (detection precondition) of the claimed production benefit.

notes: Full text available, though the Materials and Methods pages are garbled by overlapping two-column text; content is still readable. Study is leaf-scale, single region (PACA, France), single season (2016, two campaigns), four grapevine varieties, SVM 10-fold cross-validation without reported dispersion.
